chapter: Early years and the Sonny South
title: How George Augustine hired him, rehearsals and WWL broadcasts
summary: Augustine heard him at the Midway and hired him as a rhythm man. The band began broadcasting on WWL, though they made no records.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well, we were just organized at that time, you see. Well, to get back to George August there, that's how did he get to his band. So I hired him out playing at the Midway in Harvard, you see. And I hired him to play with us. And he liked the way I played. And he said, man, you're the kind of man I need. I had a fellow playing at this band, under the name of Aston Murray. But he was mostly of lead, you know. He plays lead and didn't give him no support. And so he was a man like supporting the band, you know. And he found out how to read orchestrations and things like that. And he said, you're the man that you need somebody to give the band support. At that time, you know, a lot of guys, leads all through the music, they didn't want that. They had enough instruments for solo work and things like that. So mostly he wanted a man to work for the rhythm. Yeah, a rhythm man. So he liked my playing. So he told me that I said, give me your address and say, I'm not promising anything right now, I said, but in the near future, if anything happens to the other fellow, I'll be glad to have you. About six or seven months after that, he called me up. He told me to come to rehearsal and I went and started rehearsing with him. But we didn't have too much weight then because we just had organized, you see. So I started rehearsing with him, then Pierron started getting us a little job. And Pierron started getting us a little job working as him. And finally, we started broadcasting at WWWL, Coast to Coast, and that just brought us up.
Hmm, that's something, Coast to Coast. Yeah, Coast to Coast, yeah. I don't know, I lost those records.

I wanted to always keep them, you know, before the clips, you see. Oh, you had records? I had records of it from the station, Captain Pritchett was at the head of WWL at that time. Anybody know him, Captain Pritchett? No, I haven't. He was on Tulane, I mean, yeah, Tulane. You remember the school up there?
That's where I work at Tulane.
Yeah, you remember what I mean, my school. And Loyola. Yeah, used to broadcast from Loyola at that time.
I don't have to tell you. Well, you had the records from that? That's the thing.
Well, I had some telegrams and things from different parts, you know, different parts of the states, different states, you know. Oh, yeah.
But did you record? No, not at that time.
No, you didn't make any discs?
I didn't make no discs, no.
